prompt: Tight and crowded in a low cellar print shop, a 40mm lens at chest height. Front and centre, face filling almost half the frame, a stooped Jewish printer of 70 with wild white hair, deep creases, large ears, a long nose and a few worn teeth, clean-shaven, ink-black apron over a collarless shirt, sings straight at us. A green glass-shaded lamp hanging just above the lens lights his face and mouth in sickly green. Behind him a counterfeit press burns orange, curling blank sheets lifting off it. At his shoulders, further back and smaller: a skinny young Black apprentice of 18, big-eyed, sleeves rolled, beating at flames with a rag; a beefy red-faced Irish American of 45 with a broken nose, hauling on the press lever. Thanks.
